title: Lights & Horn: When to Use Them
whatItIs: Lights help you see and be seen; the horn warns others you are there. Both have rules about when to use them.

keyFacts.text: At night you MUST use headlights, except on roads with lit street lights.
You MUST NOT use lights in a way that dazzles or bothers other road users.
You MUST use headlights when visibility is seriously reduced, usually under 100 metres.
You MUST NOT use fog lights unless visibility is seriously reduced.
You MUST NOT use your horn while stationary, or in a built-up area from 11.30 pm to 7 am, unless there is danger.

items.title: Dipped headlights
items.text: At night in built-up areas, and in dull weather so others can see you.

items.title: Main beam
items.text: Never let it dazzle others. When overtaking, stay dipped until you're level.

items.title: Fog lights
items.text: Only when you can't see more than about 100 m. Off when it clears.

items.title: Hazard warning lights
items.text: Stopped and blocking traffic, or briefly on a motorway or unrestricted dual carriageway.

items.title: Horn
items.text: Only while moving, to warn others you are there. Never in anger.

items.title: Flashing headlights
items.text: Only to let others know you are there. Not to say "go".

b.label: Fog lights
points: Switch off as soon as it clears

onTheTest.question: When may you use front or rear fog lights?
options: To warn of a hazard ahead
onTheTest.why: Fog lights are only for when visibility is seriously reduced, generally under 100 metres. Otherwise they dazzle others and hide your brake lights.

traps: Fog lights used when visibility isn't seriously reduced dazzle others and can hide your brake lights.
Don't let your lights dazzle anyone. When overtaking, keep dipped until you are level with the other vehicle.
The horn is a warning, not a way to tell people off.
